# Tactical and structural invalidation

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED -->
## Definition

Entry and hold specifications separate a horizon-appropriate tactical stop from broader structural failure. An excessively wide structural boundary cannot be relabeled as a convenient tactical stop, and stops cannot be widened to keep a losing position alive. A completed-close thesis boundary is also distinct from an executable fill.[^stock-entry-strategy-5-instructions-51bfbec68204b2d3][^stock-entry-strategy-10-instructions-b62891c31dd14f64][^stock-hold-strategy-5-instructions-d8721315f9cdba99][^stock-hold-strategy-10-instructions-d9a1481b76debebd]

## Distinct dated contexts

BULL’s September 25 5dd detailed report derives an indicative 376 closing limit from an ambiguous ATR-stop feature. Its separate 10dd report uses a close below 380 as thesis invalidation and expressly cannot define an executable stop. These are different horizon-specific framings and are retained with separate citations.[^bull-b65b7de46fe80d87][^bull-270816fba3cce331]

HRTA’s roughly 2,070 risk boundary is too wide for the 5dd Moderate entry report; the report does not invent a tighter limit. MINA separates a below-230 completed-close invalidation from the deeper 218 risk reference, which is not a guaranteed tactical exit.[^hrta-e2f2954f5612304b][^mina-b3a41fc7cf56b70d][^mina-37f439e72a0ebb94]

GPSO’s detailed/entry documents preserve 250 as a closing boundary while exact stop-fill price remains unavailable. Its hold report calls the historical below-250 rule tactical and supplies no separate structural invalidation; that terminology difference is preserved rather than silently standardized.[^gpso-d737030d107af0ac][^gpso-c8b53800c8dec568][^gpso-0e7ee5751fd4bce3]

BNBR distinguishes loss of closing support 80 from indicative ATR-derived 76. The entry report can set provisional risk arithmetic, but continued negative flow below 80 is a separate thesis-failure rule.[^bnbr-a50512c7bd8186ed][^bnbr-694cd85cde8d5c1b]

> Synthesis: Numerical agreement alone does not make two risk levels interchangeable. Rule convention, horizon, derivation, volatility and execution assumptions determine the meaning of each boundary.
